threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You say 'thank you' to the bus driver. The locals just nod, like it's a covert sign of respect in the game of commuting.
Last night on the 59, a guy argued with his imaginary friend about the best chicken shop in Brixton. Only in South London, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was part of Neukölln was when I heard two kids arguing over who could jump higher off the local playground swings—not a care in the world.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a currywurst stand sharing space with an artisanal cheese shop. Street food meets gourmet, and the lines tell you it's an experience.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: True locals know to avoid BART after 8pm on game nights. The way tourists cram in, it’s like watching a game without knowing the rules.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 49 last night, the driver yelled 'Keep your dogs off the seats, folks!' just as a guy with a chihuahua sat down. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the ‘Gràcia vibe’ is all about the plazas, but it’s really about the street corners where locals just nod and share a quiet moment.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they’re new when they still call it 'Barcelona' instead of 'Barna' and look confused at the late dinner hours.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's normal to call the tube the 'Underground.' Everyone here just calls it the 'tube' like it’s a mate.
Last night on the N35, a guy serenaded everyone with a ukulele. Never thought I'd hear 'Wonderwall' at 3 AM while passing the Ritzy.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a street musician playing a didgeridoo while a kid painted graffiti of a cat in a tutu. That blend is pure Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a late-night karaoke bar in an old laundromat. Singing among spinning washing machines is a vibe you won't forget.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're local when they know to avoid BART during a game night but still complain about the 14-Mission being late again.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in the Tenderloin serenading the bus with a ukulele. Everyone was either vibing or pretending not to listen. Classic Muni moment.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists rave about the Gaudí sights but miss the real gems like the local cafés on Carrer de Verdi, where the real Gràcia vibe lives.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fascinated by the little paper menus at local tapas bars, asking for recommendations, while everyone else just orders the usual patatas bravas.
